key_insight: DInf-Grid replaces costly coordinate-based MLP neural solvers with a differentiable feature grid representation that trains much faster while enabling accurate computation of the derivatives required to solve differential equations.
problem_solved: Coordinate-based MLP solvers (e.g., sinusoidal networks) are computationally intensive and slow to train; existing grid-based alternatives are faster but rely on simple linear interpolation, which limits accurate derivative computation needed for differential equation solvers.
method: Introduce a differentiable feature grid that stores learned local features and supports differentiable interpolation to evaluate fields and their derivatives efficiently.

Integrate the feature grid with a neural differential-equation solver so derivative evaluations used in forward/backward integration come directly from the grid representation, reducing compute and training time.
Use a compact neural head / residual component (hybrid design) and multiresolution grid strategies to capture fine-scale structure while keeping inference and optimization efficient.
impact: Enables faster, lower-cost neural solvers for ODEs/PDEs that still deliver accurate derivative estimates — making neural differential-equation methods more practical for scientific computing, simulation, and real-time applications.
visual_elements: Side-by-side diagram: coordinate-based MLP pipeline vs DInf-Grid pipeline (highlight compute and data flow differences).
Schematic of the differentiable feature grid showing learned features, interpolation kernel, and derivative extraction.
Performance chart: training time and accuracy (error) comparison between MLP solvers, linear-grid baselines, and DInf-Grid.
Field visualization: example solved PDE/ODE field and its derivative (gradient) to show improved fidelity at high frequencies.
paper_title: DInf-Grid: A Neural Differential Equation Solver with Differentiable Feature Grids
paper_authors: Navami Kairanda, Shanthika Naik, Marc Habermann, Avinash Sharma, Christian Theobalt
